question: open #2 - Does filling earthquake_curve under type_ABC=VIE cause double excitation (base acceleration superposed on the incident wave)?
registered_before: any solver run of any ablated deck; no variant deck existed on disk at registration time
source_claim_under_test: 02-facts-semantic-drift.md section 1: Fem.f90:8525 reads earthquake_curve unconditionally; 8682-8687 computes fachv from it with no type_ABC guard; fachv is applied at 13553/13852/14164/14272 with no type_ABC guard. Therefore under VIE a filled earthquake_curve adds a base acceleration on top of the incident wave.

instrument.solver_entry: fem-chat/harness/_solve_deck.py (same path as the benchmark suite); ./hstar is never called directly
instrument.workdir: /tmp/claude-1000/probe-vie/<run>/ ; cases/ is read-only, never run in place
instrument.deck_edit: ONLY line 2 of 1.man (the record 'nincs, cdtest, earthquake_curve(1:ndimn)'), tokens 3 and 4. No other byte of any input file is changed.
instrument.pre_run_cleanup: delete 1.flavia.res, 1max.flavia.res, 1.chk, run*.log, result_b*.vtp from the copy before solving
instrument.probe_node: the node of 1.cor with maximum y; ties broken by minimum x (train10 -> y=110; train02 -> y=50; vie -> y=40)
instrument.series: U(t) = (ux, uy) of the probe node, read from every 'DISPLACEMENT' block of 1.flavia.res, in file order

metrics.rms_x: sqrt(mean over output steps of ux^2)
metrics.fachv_max_1: max over all 'fachv=' lines in 1.chk of |first component|
metrics.fachv_max_2: max over all 'fachv=' lines in 1.chk of |second component|

runs.t10_base_rep: byte-identical second copy of t10_base, solved in a separate directory
runs.t10_var: train10_dynamic_vie with earthquake_curve = 2 0 (curve 2 = the SEISMIC acceleration curve in 1.LOA); everything else identical
runs.vie_var: cases/vie with earthquake_curve = 2 0 (curve 2 = SEISMIC acceleration in 1.loa)

predictions.claim: Positive control on known behaviour: in a FIX-boundary dynamic case (train02_gravdam_seismic, whose correct configuration is documented in CLAUDE.md/PRJ-6057), toggling earthquake_curve off must both silence fachv and materially change the crest response. This proves the whole instrument chain (copy -> one-slot edit -> solve -> extract) actually moves the physics.
predictions.falsified_if: NOT ( fachv_max_2(t02_on) > 0 AND fachv_max_1(t02_on) == 0 AND fachv_max_1(t02_off) == 0 AND fachv_max_2(t02_off) == 0 AND reldiff_y(t02_off vs t02_on) >= 0.10 )
predictions.note: train02's driven direction is slot 2 (y), so the fachv and displacement criteria are stated on component 2 / uy. reldiff_y is reldiff with ux replaced by uy.

predictions.claim: Determinism control: the same deck solved twice in two separate sandbox directories produces a bit-identical crest displacement series. Without this, any observed difference could be run-to-run noise rather than the ablation.
predictions.tolerance: exact equality of the decimal strings for all 250 output steps, both components
predictions.falsified_if: any output step of t10_base_rep differs in either component from t10_base, or the two runs produce a different number of DISPLACEMENT blocks

predictions.claim: With earthquake_curve = 0 0 under VIE, fachv stays identically zero for the whole run: the base-acceleration path is dormant in the baseline deck.

CORE, mechanism half: with earthquake_curve = 2 0 and type_ABC still VIE, fachv becomes non-zero. i.e. the fachv computation at Fem.f90:8682-8687 really has no type_ABC guard and VIE does not suppress it.
predictions.falsified_if: the t10_var run fails to produce 1.flavia.res, or fachv_max_1(t10_var) == 0

predictions.claim: CORE, physics half: the non-zero fachv actually reaches the equation of motion under VIE, so the crest x-displacement history changes materially versus the baseline. Double excitation is real, not merely a value computed and discarded.

The added path is additive in magnitude, not cancelling: the variant's peak |ux| at the crest is strictly larger than the baseline's. (This is the weakest of the set - superposition of two excitations could in principle partly cancel at the peak instant.)

Replication on the second, independent VIE case (cases/vie, a different mesh, different curve file, 1500 steps): the same one-slot edit reproduces both halves - fachv becomes non-zero and the crest x-history changes by at least 5%. A single-case result would not distinguish 'VIE has no guard' from 'train10 is peculiar'.
predictions.falsified_if: fachv_max_1(vie_var) == 0, or reldiff_x < 0.05, or either vie run fails to produce 1.flavia.res

known_limitations_declared_in_advance: train10's absorbing boundary is itself defective (30 vertical edges mislabelled as bottom boundary, per 02-facts-semantic-drift.md section 4). Both runs of the ablation pair use the SAME defective boundary, so the pair remains a valid ablation; but the absolute displacement values of either run are not trustworthy physics.
This probe tests whether the second excitation path is ACTIVE under VIE. It does not test which of the two excitations is physically correct, nor quantify the error a user would make.

Curve 2 is chosen as 'the acceleration curve' because it is the SEISMIC-typed curve in both LOA files; that identification is read off the deck, not independently verified against the solver's curve indexing.
